# 2 Maccabees Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** Very shortly after this, Lysias the king's guardian and kinsman and administrator of the affairs of state, being greatly displeased at what had happened, gathered about eighty thousand soldiers and all his cavalry and came against the Jews.

**11:2** His purpose was to make the city a Greek settlement and to impose a tax on the temple, as on the other sacred places of the nations, and to put the high priesthood up for sale each year.

**11:3** He took no account at all of the power of God, but was puffed up in his tens of thousands of infantry and thousands of cavalry and eighty elephants.

**11:4** So he entered Judea and drew near to Beth-zur, a strong place about five stadia from Jerusalem, and besieged it.

**11:5** But when Maccabeus and his men learned that he was besieging the fortifications, they and all the people lamented with wailing and tears, begging the Lord to send a good angel to save Israel.

**11:6** Maccabeus himself was the first to take up arms, and he urged the others to risk their lives along with him to aid their fellow countrymen. And they all set out together with passionate eagerness.

**11:7** And while they were still near Jerusalem, a horseman appeared at their head clothed in white and brandishing golden weapons.

**11:8** And they all together praised the merciful God, and were strengthened in their hearts, ready to assault not only men but the most savage beasts and walls of iron.

**11:9** They advanced in battle order with their heavenly ally, since the Lord had shown mercy to them.

**11:10** And hurling themselves like lions against the enemy, they cut down eleven thousand infantry and sixteen hundred cavalry, and forced all the rest to flee.

**11:11** Most of them escaped wounded; and Lysias himself fled in a disgraceful manner, having escaped with his bare life.

**11:12** And he was not without intelligence; for he considered within himself the loss that had come about, and understood that the Hebrews were invincible because the mighty God fought on their side. Therefore he sent to them

**11:13** and persuaded them to settle everything on just terms, promising to persuade the king as well about all things that were necessary to be favorable to them.

**11:14** And Maccabeus agreed to all that Lysias asked, attending to the common good; and whatever Maccabeus wrote to Lysias concerning the Jews, the king granted.

**11:15** For there were letters written to the Jews from Lysias containing the following words:

**11:16** "Lysias to the people of the Jews, greetings. John and Absalom, who were sent from you, handed over the document written below and asked for the fulfillment of the matters mentioned in it.

**11:17** Whatever it was necessary to bring before the king, I have stated; and what was admissible he has agreed to.

**11:18** If you will maintain goodwill toward the government, I will endeavor to contribute to your prosperity in the future.

**11:19** And on the particular matters and their detail I have instructed both these men and my own representatives to confer with you.

**11:20** Farewell. In the year one hundred forty-eight, on the twenty-fourth of Dioscorinthius."

**11:21** The king's letter contained the following:

**11:22** "King Antiochus to his brother Lysias, greetings. Since our father was translated to the gods, it is our wish that the subjects of our kingdom be undisturbed in attending to their own affairs.

**11:23** We have heard that the Jews cannot consent to our father's change to Greek ways, but prefer their own manner of living and request that they be allowed their own customs.

**11:24** Therefore we choose that this nation also should be at peace, and our decision is that their temple be restored to them and that they live according to the customs of their ancestors.

**11:25** You will therefore do well to send word to them and give them pledges of friendship, so that, knowing our will, they may be of good spirit and with a light heart attend to the conduct of their own affairs."

**11:26** The letter to the Jews from the king was as follows:

**11:27** "King Antiochus to the Senate of the Jews and to the rest of the Jews, greetings. If you are in good health, it is as we wish. We ourselves also are in good health.

**11:28** Menelaus has informed us that you wish to return home and attend to your own affairs.

**11:29** Therefore those who return home by the thirtieth of Xanthicus will have the guarantee of full amnesty,

**11:30** and the Jews will be permitted to use their own food and observe their laws, just as before, and none of them will be molested in any way for things done in ignorance.

**11:31** I have also sent Menelaus to speak with you.

**11:32** Farewell. In the year one hundred forty-eight, on the fifteenth of Xanthicus."

**11:33** The Romans also sent them a letter as follows:

**11:34** "Quintus Memmius and Titus Manius, legates of the Romans, to the people of the Jews, greetings.

**11:35** With regard to what Lysias the kinsman of the king has granted you, we also give our consent.

**11:36** But as for the matters that he decided should be referred to the king, as soon as you have deliberated over them, send someone promptly so that we may present them in a manner suitable for you; for we are going to Antioch.

**11:37** Therefore make haste and send some persons so that we may know what your preference is.

**11:38** Farewell. In the year one hundred forty-eight, on the fifteenth of Xanthicus."
